summary: Adversarial two-lens review (engineering/integration and lab outcome/adoption) of the LabStock implementation plan

result.verdict:
The architecture is sound and the Quartzy facts are used correctly, but MVP-A is not buildable as written. Several silent defaults and undefined behaviours would break it in production:
- **Background jobs:** Django-Q2 re-runs any task still going after 60 s, which means duplicate syncs and duplicate emails.
- **Quartzy paging:** the page index base, sort order and stability are undefined, and `updated_at` and `requested_by` can be null.
- **Order status:** only Lab Admins can mark a request Ordered, yet the plan keys its stale nudges and post-order alerts on ORDERED.
- **Catalog numbers:** generic ones (custom oligos, services, "N/A") turn exact-match tier T1 into a false-positive generator.
- **Login:** allauth's signup is open by default, and behind Caddy its per-IP rate limits apply to the whole lab.
- **Email:** an email-only guard has no sender domain or deliverability plan.

Several MVP-A flows also have no data model: claim outcomes, ask-owner and ask-the-lab, pending claims, provisional products and merges. Ask-the-lab's "reply" quietly implies parsing inbound email.

The stack choice holds: Django 6.1 now, 6.2 LTS next. Every listed package works on 6.1 at the right minimum version except django-import-export, whose 4.4.x declares only Django ≤5.2 and whose 5.0 (adding 6.x) is unreleased. It also saves rows directly and so bypasses the stock ledger. Drop it, and drop `rules` (unmaintained since 2024-09), instead of falling back to Django 5.2.

The build order needs two changes. The Quartzy probe, normalization and baseline must come before the scaffold, because Phase 0 currently depends on build steps 3, 4 and 6. And the sync should be deployed right after it is built, so the 2–4 shadow weeks overlap UI work. Expect roughly 150–300 h for MVP-A, not 100–200 h.

Plan reviewed: /Users/Raghuram/.claude/plans/i-would-like-to-memoized-firefly.md (§4–§10).

issues.section: §5 Architecture (worker) / §7 Sync mechanics / §6 Notification
issues.problem: Django-Q2 defaults to retry=60 s and timeout=None. With the ORM broker, a task still running after 60 s is handed out again and runs a second time in parallel. The nightly full scan, the backfill, the digests and the baseline will all exceed 60 s. Two copies of a sync then race on upserts and status observations, and two copies of a send task mean every recipient gets the alert or digest twice. The plan has no guard against a job overlapping itself, no idempotent send, and no rule against sending from inside a transaction that later rolls back.
issues.fix:
Add to §5/§7:
(1) Set Q_CLUSTER = {orm: 'default', workers: 2, timeout: 600, retry: 900, max_attempts: 2, ack_failures: True}, keeping timeout < retry. Split long work into tasks of at most N pages that re-enqueue themselves with a cursor, so every task finishes well under the timeout. Run the history backfill as a management command, not a task.
(2) Run each sync job under a single-flight lock per (job, quartzy_lab): a Postgres session advisory lock released in `finally`, or a JobLease row with an expiry. Skip the run if the lock is taken.
(3) Give Notification a UniqueConstraint on (kind, subject_type, subject_id, recipient) as its idempotency key. Enqueue sends with transaction.on_commit. The send task does select_for_update, checks that sent_at IS NULL, sends, then stores the ESP message id.
(4) Pass only ids as task arguments. Q2 stores arguments in an admin-visible table.
(5) Test: run the sync and send tasks twice concurrently and assert exactly one email and an identical set of observations.
issues.evidence: django-q2 configure docs: retry 'Defaults to 60 … Django-Q2 will start the task again if the used broker supports receipts' (their sleep(22) with retry 5 ran 5 times); timeout 'Defaults to None'. https://django-q2.readthedocs.io/en/master/configure.html

issues.section: §7 Sync cadence & mechanics; §4 Phase 0 step 3 (spike)
issues.problem:
The cadence rests on facts the spec leaves undefined, and it misses several verified edge cases.
- **Page base:** `page` has no declared base, default or minimum. Starting at the wrong index silently skips or repeats a page, and with newest-first order the skipped page is the newest one.
- **Offset paging:** results are bare arrays, so a request inserted or deleted mid-scan shifts items between pages. Missing from a full scan does not mean deleted.
- **Nullable fields:** `updated_at`, `requested_by` and `User.email` can all be null, so `updated_at` can't be the change detector.
- **Call budget:** refreshing every open request by id costs one call per open request per cycle. About 100 open requests twice an hour is already ~200 of the 300 calls/h budget. It also misses reverts on closed requests (Admins can revert Received → New) until the nightly scan.
- **Strict models:** pydantic models generated from a spec full of additionalProperties:false will reject responses the day Quartzy adds a field, and the API is unversioned. One malformed record, such as a non-numeric quantity string, can abort a page.
- **Money units:** `total_price.amount` has format 'integer' with an undocumented unit, while `unit_price` is a plain string. A cents-vs-dollars mistake puts a 100× error into the baseline and the '$ avoided' figure.
- **Sort order:** if results aren't in time order, polling can't find new requests within 5 minutes, and webhooks (which need inbound HTTPS) become an MVP-A dependency.
issues.fix:
Rewrite §7 'Sync cadence'. Every 5 minutes, for each QuartzyLab returned by GET /labs that maps to the app's lab, under that lab's lock:
(a) Head probe: read from the measured insertion end, continuing while a page contains unknown ids, up to 5 pages.
(b) Rolling sweep: read the next 2–4 pages of the full list from a saved cursor, so all history is re-read every few hours. Example: ~4,000 requests at 25 per page comes to ~50–70 calls/h in total.
(c) Refresh by id only a 'hot set': requests with an alert, outcome or cancel verification pending.

Rules for every pass:
- Detect changes with a sha256 of the canonical payload; treat updated_at only as a hint. Each observation stores quartzy_updated_at.
- Treat a request as deleted only after GET /order-requests/{id} returns 404. Then set deleted_in_quartzy_at; never delete the row.
- If more than 5% of the ids checked in one run return 404, abort and alert. That pattern means a token or permission change, not deletions.
- Use permissive response models (extra='allow'), keep the raw payload, log unknown fields, and catch errors per record into a SyncError table.

Add these checks to the Phase 0 spike, each pinned by a fixture test:
- whether page indexing starts at 0 or 1, and what omitting it does
- page size
- sort key, and whether the same page returns the same order twice
- which page a new request lands on
- whether editing an old request moves it
- whether a deleted request returns 404 (in a sandbox)
- the Money unit: total_price.amount vs unit_price × quantity vs the UI
- requested_by vs created_by on requests made on someone's behalf, and how QBot requests appear
- whether GET /labs lists every Quartzy Lab that people actually use

Contingency: if there is no usable time order, register the order-request.created webhook (this needs the Phase 0 hostname) and keep polling as reconciliation.
issues.evidence: public-api.yaml: page is 'type integer', no default or minimum; no response headers; OrderRequest.updated_at is nullable; OrderRequestWithType.requested_by is nullable; Money.amount has format integer; unit_price is a string. Verification: order-request.deleted covers Admin hard-deletes only; 'Admins can revert … from Received all the way back to New'.

issues.section: §7 Sync mechanics (first-run backfill) / §6 PolicySetting
issues.problem: The rule 'alert only when requested_at is within a few hours of first_seen_at' covers the first backfill and nothing else. (a) After a worker or Quartzy outage, say a weekend, requests created during the gap are silently never alerted. (b) A burst passes the rule, for example someone entering 30 lines, or a Quartzy order-history Excel import whose rows carry the import time. (c) There is no global kill switch and no cap per cycle, so a bad vendor rule or a matcher bug emails the whole lab before anyone notices. An alert storm in week one is the fastest way to lose the lab.
issues.fix:
Replace the rule in §7:
- **Arming:** add QuartzyLab.alerts_armed_at, set when the backfill completes and the tier goes live. Alert only when requested_at ≥ alerts_armed_at.
- **Late detections:** a request first seen more than PolicySetting.late_after (e.g. 6 h) after requested_at gets the post-order wording and goes into the next digest instead of being dropped.
- **Burst hold:** more than N new requests (e.g. 8) from one creator within 15 minutes are held for the system owner to review.
- **Circuit breaker:** if one cycle produces more than M alerts (e.g. 10), hold them all and email the system owner a one-tap release.
- **Kill switches:** PolicySetting.alerts_enabled, global and per tier, checked at send time.
- **Tests:** a time-machine test for each rule.
issues.evidence: The research shows Quartzy's order-history Excel import creates rows in New or Ordered (support article 233421567). Neither the critique's fix nor the plan covers outage gaps or bursts.

issues.section: §4 Phase 0 step 2 and MVP-A in-flight board / stale nudges; §7 post-order alert variant
issues.problem:
Quartzy's verified role rules:
- only Lab Admins can mark a request Ordered
- Members can cancel only their own requests, and only while they are New
- both roles can mark Received

In a lab with no approver where everyone orders, Members' requests probably go straight from CREATED to RECEIVED, or stay CREATED after the vendor order is placed. The plan keys four things on ORDERED: stale nudges (ORDERED > 21 days), the Phase 0 cleanup (ORDERED/BACKORDERED > 60 days), the post-order alert variant, and the in-flight board.

If the spike confirms this pattern, stale CREATED rows clog 'On order' and the matcher, the post-order rescue never fires, and the alert offers 'I'll cancel' to people who can't cancel. Partial receipts also stay ORDERED, and the API has no received quantity.
issues.fix:
(1) Spike: from history, measure the mix of status paths (% that ever reach ORDERED, % that go CREATED → RECEIVED), the age of open requests by status, and the Quartzy roles of the token owner and the members.
(2) Apply the Phase 0 cleanup and stale nudges to every open status (CREATED, APPROVED, ORDERED, BACKORDERED), with per-status age thresholds in PolicySetting.
(3) The alert never infers 'already purchased' from status. It asks 'Already placed with the vendor?' Not yet → 'I'll cancel in Quartzy' (deep link). Already ordered → 'cancel with vendor / return' or 'keep & offer surplus'.
(4) The in-flight board labels CREATED requests older than N days as 'requested, not marked ordered'.
(5) The matcher shows open candidates older than 60 days as 'probably arrived, still open in Quartzy'.
(6) Claim lists add 'Did this arrive?' for CREATED/ORDERED requests older than 30 days.
issues.evidence: Verification claim 9 (article 115000426253): Mark Ordered is Admin-only; Members can cancel only their own New requests; both roles can Mark Received. Claim 49: without approvals, New goes to Ordered. Claim 65: partial receipts stay ORDERED, and the payload has no received quantity.

issues.section: §4 MVP-A Product identity; §7 Matching tiers (T1); catalog normalization
issues.problem:
T1 treats an exact catalog_key as the same product, and across vendors whenever the key has 7 or more characters. Quartzy history will contain catalog numbers that identify nothing:
- placeholders: N/A, '-', TBD, 'see notes', 'custom'
- vendor-generic numbers reused for different items: custom oligos, gBlocks and gene synthesis, sequencing services, custom peptides and antibodies, shipping and dry-ice fees

With the current identity rule, every IDT primer becomes one Product:
- T1 flags every pair of primer orders that are open at the same time.
- 'Bought before' shows 300 or more past purchases of 'the same' item.
- Claim-your-history collapses dozens of tubes into one row.
- Pair suppression can't help, because both sides are the same SupplierProduct.

The cross-vendor rule also lets unrelated numeric SKUs from different vendor families collide. Requests with no catalog # get no guard at all, since T4 is search-only, and nothing reports how many such requests there are.
issues.fix:
(1) In normalization.py, map placeholder values from a stop-list to catalog_key = NULL.
(2) Add SupplierProduct.identity = identifying | generic, and ItemType.identity_rule='none' for oligo, service and fee Types. Requests on a generic SupplierProduct each get their own provisional Product and are never grouped by catalog #. Oligos are left to the v1 sequence matching.
(3) Cross-vendor-family T1 requires the same ItemType or a minimum name similarity (trigram ≥0.2). Report it as a separate tier, T1x, so shadow mode measures it on its own.
(4) Seed the generic list from the Phase 0 export: catalog keys with many distinct item_names.
(5) Show on the health panel and the dashboard the share of requests the guard can't check (missing or generic catalog #).
issues.evidence: Synthesis note: 'Requests with no catalog number are matched on name and type only', but the plan makes T4 search-only, so those requests are never alerted. The verification found no catalog-number normalization or validation on Quartzy's side.

issues.section: §5 Libraries (allauth); §8 step 2 Core; §7 Credentials
issues.problem:
QR labels and email links need a hostname that phones can reach, so the app will be internet-facing. That exposes four gaps.
- **Open signup:** allauth's signup is open by default (DefaultAccountAdapter.is_open_for_signup returns True), so anyone could register and browse who has what where.
- **Admin login:** Django admin's login skips allauth's rate limits and MFA. The plan gives staff no MFA until v1, yet staff can edit everything.
- **Proxy IPs:** behind Caddy, allauth 65.14.2+ no longer trusts X-Forwarded-For, and ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT defaults to 0. Every user then appears as Caddy's IP, so the per-IP limits (login 30/m/ip, login_failed 10/m/ip) become lab-wide lockouts. allauth also keeps its counters in a cache, and LocMemCache is per Gunicorn worker, so the counts are inconsistent.
- **Quartzy token:** it is unscoped. If its owner is a Lab Admin, which is likely when everyone orders, one bug could cancel or approve real requests.
issues.fix:
Add to step 2:
- A custom account adapter with is_open_for_signup=False. A management command provisions accounts and Membership rows from a roster CSV. Login-by-code works only for active members.
- admin.site.login = secure_admin_login(admin.site.login).
- Require allauth MFA (TOTP) for is_staff from MVP-A, using a small middleware that sends staff without an authenticator to MFA setup. Add passkeys once the hostname is permanent, because WebAuthn is bound to it.
- Optionally, restrict /admin to campus or VPN ranges in Caddy.
- Set ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT=1 (or a trusted header that Caddy sets), SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS.
- Use Django's DatabaseCache (createcachetable; no Redis) for the allauth rate limits and Q2 stats.
- The Quartzy client's HTTP transport refuses anything but GET, with a unit test. Record the token owner's Quartzy role in the runbook.
issues.evidence: allauth admin docs: the admin login 'is not protected from being brute forced (ACCOUNT_RATE_LIMITS)' and 2FA is not enforced; workaround secure_admin_login (https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/common/admin.html). Rate-limit defaults: login 30/m/ip, login_failed 10/m/ip,5/5m/key (https://docs.allauth.org/en/latest/account/rate_limits.html). 65.14.2 stopped trusting XFF; ALLAUTH_TRUSTED_PROXY_COUNT defaults to 0 (https://docs.allauth.org/en/dev/common/rate_limits.html).

issues.section: §6 StockItem visibility / Hold; §5 Libraries (rules); §7 alert content; §4 digests
issues.problem:
Visibility is defined, but the only enforcement named is 'rules (object permissions)'. rules answers yes or no per object. It doesn't filter querysets or redact individual fields, yet a restricted item has to stay visible (it exists, and here is whom to ask) while its location is hidden.

Most leak paths are not pages: the duplicate alert ('what matched, where, whose'), the Monday digest, ask-owner and ask-the-lab emails, the PI dashboard, CSV export, htmx partials, the admin changelist, and Q2 task arguments.

'Reserved' is defined twice, as a visibility value and as a Hold type. rules 3.5 (2024-09-02) declares no Django versions and Python only up to 3.12.
issues.fix:
Add inventory/presenters.py with present_item(item, viewer, channel) → dict. It redacts location, position and notes for each combination of visibility and viewer role (custodian, PI/admin, member, recipient of a signed link).
- Every template, email, digest, CSV and serializer renders only presenter output.
- A test greps templates for direct item.location access.
- A matrix test runs a restricted fixture through every renderer and viewer role and asserts the location string never appears.
- All querysets go through StockItem.objects.for_lab(lab).
- visibility = shared / ask-first / restricted; reservations exist only as Holds.
- Replace rules with plain predicate functions in apps/core/permissions.py.
issues.evidence: PyPI rules: latest 3.5 (2024-09-02); no 'Framework :: Django ::' version classifiers; Python classifiers stop at 3.12. The critique asked for restricted items to 'hide their location while still showing that they exist and whom to ask'.

issues.section: §2 Notifications / Hosting; §4 Phase 0; §12 Open items
issues.problem:
The guard, claims, asks and digests all go by email, but hosting is deferred to MVP-B.
- Plain SMTP from a cloud VM is usually blocked or junked.
- A university relay usually needs the server on campus and may restrict the From address.
- University Microsoft 365/Defender quarantines link-heavy mail from new domains.

The hostname is also an MVP-A need, not just an MVP-B label issue:
- every alert carries signed links with the host baked in
- the webhook fallback needs inbound HTTPS
- passkeys bind to the hostname

If alerts land in junk, the guard does nothing, and the shadow metrics won't show why.
issues.fix:
Phase 0:
- Register a lab-controlled domain, or get a permanent university subdomain whose CNAME you control. app.<domain> becomes the QR base, the link host and the sender domain.
- Send through an ESP's HTTPS API via anymail (Postmark, SES or Mailgun). This works from any host.
- Publish SPF and DKIM, and a DMARC record starting at p=none.
- Ask IT to allowlist the sender in M365 and, if they allow it, exempt it from Safe Links rewriting.
- Seed-test inbox placement in Gmail and the university mailbox before shadow mode starts.
- Store ESP message ids and track bounces.

MVP-A then runs on any temporary host behind that DNS name. Moving hosts later means a restore plus a DNS change, so the monthly restore drill doubles as migration practice. Use Caddy's DNS-01 challenge if the host has no inbound 80/443.
issues.evidence: Tech research gotchas: 'University VMs often have no inbound internet, so Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 fails; use DNS-01'; 'Phones off campus may need VPN if the VM isn't public'.

issues.section: §6 StockEvent / StockItem; §5 Frontend (admin as back office); §9 Privacy (retention); §10 ledger invariants
issues.problem:
The plan says every stock change goes through one service function, but nothing in the code enforces it. The Django admin is the steward's back office, so the first admin edit of location, custodian or lifecycle silently breaks 'current state = fold of events'. QuerySet.update() and treebeard subtree moves, which rewrite paths in SQL without signals, break it the same way.
- Nothing serializes concurrent changes to one item: two taps, an htmx retry and a sync event.
- client_uuid isn't declared unique.
- Ordering events by `at` breaks for backdated events, which claim-your-history creates when it records receipts from months ago.
- §9's 'retention period for event logs' contradicts §10's fold invariant: deleting events changes the computed state.
issues.fix:
inventory.services.apply_event(item_id, event, expected_version) does all of this in one transaction:
- select_for_update on the StockItem
- reject a stale expected_version ('changed since you opened this')
- append the StockEvent with a per-item seq, unique on (stock_item, seq)
- update the cached fields and bump the version

Supporting rules:
- A UniqueConstraint on client_uuid where it is not null.
- Separate occurred_at (may be backdated) from recorded_at, and fold by seq.
- Admin: state fields are read-only and change only through admin actions that call the service.
- StockItem.save() raises if a state field changed outside the service (a contextvar flag); a test asserts the admin form has no state fields.
- Retention means pseudonymizing StockEvent.user after N months, never deleting events.
- Location moves write a LocationEvent.
- MVP-B: Django can't make the partial unique constraint on active positions deferrable, so position swaps are two-step moves in the service.
issues.evidence: The plan makes the admin the 'back office for the system owner / data steward' (§5), while §10 tests that 'current state = fold of events' and §9 sets 'a retention period for event logs'.

issues.section: §4 MVP-A Claim your history / Check-before-you-buy actions; §6 Data model
issues.problem:
§6 has no models for three MVP-A flows:
- claim-your-history: one-tap outcomes, monthly rounds, 'Gave to X', how many are left
- ask-owner
- ask-the-lab and its pending claims

'An I-have-it reply creates a pending claim' comes from the research's chat-channel design. Under email-only, a reply means parsing inbound mail: an ESP inbound webhook (needs public HTTPS) or IMAP polling. That is an unplanned feature tied to the hosting decision.

An email to a list address can't carry per-person signed links, so a click can't be attributed to anyone. StockItem.lifecycle also has no state for 'someone says they have it, unconfirmed'.
issues.fix:
Add to §6:
- **HistoryClaim:** order_request, person, outcome (have_it / used_up / gave_to / not_mine / snoozed), count_kept, target_person, stock_items (M2M), decided_at, round. Unique on (order_request, person).
- **AskThread:** kind (owner / lab), asker, query_text, product (optional), stock_item (optional), closed_at.
- **AskReply:** thread, responder, answer (have_it / can_lend / used_up / not_mine / no), stock_item (optional).
- **Lifecycle 'unverified':** search shows 'probably — ask X'; excluded from availability; confirmed or rejected through services.

Ask-the-lab sends one email per active member, each with personal signed buttons (I have it / Maybe / No) and Reply-To set to the asker. Free-text answers go person to person; MVP-A does no inbound parsing. Rate-limit asks per person per day.
issues.evidence: Critique standout idea: 'one tap posts "Does anyone have X?" to the lab channel. An "I have it" reply creates a pending record' (chat-based). The plan turned this into 'an email to the lab list … an "I have it" reply creates a pending claim'.

issues.section: §4 MVP-A Product identity; §6 Catalog / Lot
issues.problem:
Claims, imports and the guard all need StockItem.product, and Lot is keyed on (product, lot_number). Yet MVP-A resolves products only through an admin queue that never auto-merges, with no rule for unresolved requests. Hundreds of historical requests would block claim-your-history until someone resolves them by hand, or Claude Code will invent ad-hoc product creation.

Manual merges are certain, and the plan has no merge mechanism. A merge must:
- re-point SupplierProducts, StockItems, OrderRequests, DuplicateMatches and PairSuppressions
- handle Lots, where (product, lot_number) will collide
- keep the links in already-sent alerts working

Two more gaps:
- Vendor strings that don't resolve ('Amazon', 'core facility') have no VendorFamily for the unique (vendor_family, catalog_key).
- Distributor SKUs that differ from the manufacturer's number (VWR, and Fisher's own codes) never match at T1.
issues.fix:
(1) At ingest, any request without a T1/T2 match gets a provisional Product (provisional=True). An unknown vendor string also gets a provisional Vendor/VendorFamily. Both go to the review queue.
(2) Add Product.merged_into (a self-FK) and catalog.services.merge_products(src, dst). In one transaction it re-points every FK, merges colliding Lots, rewrites suppressions and writes history, and it leaves src as a redirect. Do the same for vendors.
(3) Normalize lot_number into lot_key and key Lot on (product, lot_key).
(4) Add nullable SupplierProduct.mfr_family and mfr_catalog_key, filled from vendor rules or the review queue, and let T1 match on either key.
(5) Test merges against a fixture that has lots and suppressions.
issues.evidence: Critique data_model_issues: 'Matching an OrderRequest to a Product needs an unresolved state … Merges also need redirect records so links in old alerts still work.' The plan includes the queue but not the merge mechanism or a provisional state.

issues.section: §8 Build order; §4 Phase 0 steps 3–4
issues.problem:
Phase 0 runs 'build step 4's quartzy_probe.py', and its baseline needs normalization (step 3) and the baseline analyzer (step 6). So 'weeks 0–1, mostly no code' actually depends on half of MVP-A.

Deployment is step 8, yet shadow mode needs the sync running around the clock for 2–4 weeks, and status observations only exist from the day sync starts. Starting shadow mode after step 8 adds the whole shadow period to the calendar.

The research JSON also sits in /private/tmp (cleared on reboot) until step 1.
issues.fix:
Rewrite §8:
- 0a: copy the research to docs/research/ now.
- 0b: a standalone probe (httpx only, no Django) that writes a raw JSON export to data/.
- 0c: catalog/normalization.py as pure Python with no ORM imports, plus table tests seeded from real exported strings.
- 0d: the baseline notebook, importing 0c.
- 1: scaffold.
- 2: core: roster provisioning, Membership, PersonAlias, signed-action helper.
- 3: catalog: provisional products, merge service, generic stop-list, ItemType seed with a QuartzyType→ItemType FK.
- 4: Quartzy sync.
- 5: deploy a minimal production stack (Caddy, web, worker, db, backups, external heartbeat, ESP and domain) and start the 24/7 mirror.
- 6: guard matcher in silent shadow mode plus the labelling page, run against the mirror (open requests, receipts, Quartzy inventory).
- 7: minimal inventory, claims, search and asks, built during the shadow weeks.
- 8: alerts go live tier by tier; digests; dashboard.

Add a re-estimate checkpoint after step 4.
issues.evidence: Plan §4 Phase 0.3: 'Build step 4's scripts/quartzy_probe.py runs with your token'. §8 step 6: 'baseline analyzer, shared with the notebook'. §8 step 8 (Ops) comes after the guard and UI steps.

issues.section: §5 Versions / Libraries; §4 MVP-A Spreadsheet import; §8 step 5
issues.problem:
Django 6.1 now and 6.2 LTS next is sound: 6.1 gets security fixes until Dec 2027, 6.2 LTS runs Apr 2027 to Apr 2030, and 5.2 ends in Apr 2028 without 6.0's template partials and built-in CSP. But the fallback rule ties the framework version to the weakest dependency.

django-import-export 4.4.4 declares only Django 4.2, 5.1 and 5.2. Django 6.0 support arrives in 5.0.0, which is unreleased; 4.4.4 only patches a 6.1 admin-action deprecation. Its import path also saves models directly (save_instance → instance.save()), bypassing the single stock service, so the first spreadsheet import creates StockItems with no StockEvents.

The other packages are fine at the right minimum versions:
- treebeard 7.0.3 declares 6.1 (TreeAdmin was rewritten in 7.0)
- allauth 65.21 declares 6.1
- django-q2 added 6.1 in 1.11.0
- simple-history added 6.1 in 3.12.0, though its classifiers lag
- anymail tests against 6.1 from 15.1
- RapidFuzz 3.14.6 needs Python ≥3.11

Django 6.1 also deprecates EMAIL_BACKEND and EMAIL_* in favour of MAILERS, and `check --deploy` rejects non-production backends in 'default' (mail.E001).
issues.fix:
Drop django-import-export from MVP-A. Replace it with `manage.py import_stock <canonical.csv> --custodian <user> [--commit]`, which:
- reads the canonical CSV produced by each per-person pandas cleanup
- resolves products through the catalog service
- applies every row through inventory.services inside transaction.atomic(), rolling back unless --commit is given
- writes a review CSV of proposed product, location and warnings per row

Replace the 5.2 fallback with: 'if a dependency fails on 6.1, replace the dependency, not Django.' Budget 4–8 h for the 6.2 upgrade after 6.2.1 (May–Jun 2027).

Pin minimum versions in pyproject.toml:
- Django>=6.1,<6.2
- django-allauth>=65.21
- django-q2>=1.11
- django-simple-history>=3.12
- django-treebeard>=7.0.3 (don't subclass TreeAdmin)
- django-anymail>=15.1
- requires-python '>=3.12,<3.14', using the same minor version in the Dockerfile

Configure email through MAILERS: the anymail ESP backend in production, Mailpit SMTP in dev. Keep WeasyPrint, segno and python-barcode out of the MVP-A image; WeasyPrint needs Pango/HarfBuzz apt packages when it arrives in MVP-B.
issues.evidence: PyPI django-import-export 4.4.4 classifiers: Django 4.2/5.1/5.2. issues.section: §4 Phase 0 step 4 (baseline); §6 Guard models; §7 Noise control / $ avoided; §9 shadow mode
issues.problem:
The API returns only the current status, requested_at and updated_at; it has no ordered, received or cancelled dates. The baseline's main bucket ('same # in the same Lab while open') and a historical quartzy_native_would_fire both need to know whether the earlier request was still open at the time, and the API can't say.

Shadow mode will also be thin. A 30-person lab makes perhaps 100–400 requests in 2–4 weeks, so a ≥85–90% precision target per tier and item type rests on a handful of matches per cell.

The guard models also lack what labelling and honest reporting need:
- DuplicateMatch has no label field; the requester's outcome is not the steward's judgement.
- The candidate is a generic type/id that can't be FK-protected and keeps no snapshot of what was shown.
- PairSuppression's key and scope are undefined, so one requester's tap could mute a true duplicate for everyone, forever.
- '$ avoided' would count self-reported 'I'll cancel' taps.
issues.fix:
(1) Phase 0: also pull the Quartzy UI 'All Time' requests export. Check which status-date columns it carries; the UI filters by Submitted, Approved, Ordered, Received and Cancelled dates. Join it to the API rows on (lab, item, catalog #, requester, requested date, price). If the dates are missing, label that baseline bucket 'unknown' rather than guessing.
(2) Go-live gate: label a point-in-time replay of the last 6–12 months plus the live shadow weeks. Gate per tier with a minimum sample, e.g. ≥30 labelled matches; a tier below that stays digest-only.
(3) DuplicateMatch gets:
- label (true_dup / related_not_dup / false), labelled_by and labelled_at
- candidate_snapshot as JSON
- nullable candidate_stock_item and candidate_order_request FKs, with a check constraint that exactly one is set
- a suppressed flag, so suppressed matches still count in the reports
(4) PairSuppression is keyed on (lab, product_a, product_b, ordered) or on (subject supplier_product, candidate stock_item). Its scope is the requester by default and lab-wide only when the steward promotes it, and it has an expires_at.
(5) A cancel counts toward $ avoided only after the sync sees CANCELLED, or a confirmed deletion, within N days. Otherwise it reverts to 'kept' after one reminder. Compute quartzy_native_would_fire within the same Quartzy Lab only, with both raw-exact and normalized comparisons.
issues.evidence: public-api.yaml: OrderRequest has no ordered_at, received_at or cancelled_at. Verification claim 84: the requests export filters by Submitted, Approved, Ordered, Received or Cancelled date. Verification: the UI's status history 'is not exposed by the API'.

issues.section: §6 StockItem (unique Quartzy ids); §2 Physical stock (the switch); §4 MVP-A Quartzy inventory import / Claim your history
issues.problem:
A StockItem is one container: one label, one ContainerCode, one 'Empty' button, one pack-equivalent. A Quartzy instance merges containers that share location, lot and expiry, with a quantity string such as '4', and un-migrated labs have only item-level quantities. 'Unique Quartzy item/instance ids' on StockItem forces one instance per StockItem, so 4 bottles become one row.

During the switch, the same bottle can exist both as a mirrored Quartzy item and as a claimed or imported StockItem. Order requests carry no inventory link, so claim-your-history will duplicate whatever receivers also added in Quartzy. Nothing says which side wins when both change.
issues.fix:
Keep the raw mirror (QuartzyInventoryItem / QuartzyInventoryInstance) in apps/quartzy. Link it through ExternalRef(stock_item, system, external_id), which allows many StockItems per instance.

Import rule:
- A whole-number quantity of 20 or less in pack units splits into that many StockItems, one per container.
- Anything else becomes one StockItem with tracking_mode=count and is_aggregate=True, offering 'split into containers' the first time someone touches it.

Before creating anything, the claim flow shows likely mirrored matches with a 'This is the same bottle' button. A likely match has the same catalog_key or name, added_by = the requester, and was created within 14 days after requested_at.

Set a cutover date per lab:
- Before it, Quartzy wins for source=quartzy items, applied through service events with source='quartzy'.
- After it, the app wins and Quartzy-side changes only raise drift flags on the health panel.
issues.evidence: Verification additional facts: 'Receiving into inventory creates instances automatically and merges them when location, lot and expiration match'; instance quantity is a string; order-request payloads 'carry no inventory-item id, so linking orders to inventory needs heuristic matching'.

issues.section: §6 General rules (lab FK, User status, PersonAlias); custodian
issues.problem:
Problems with tenancy:
- A lab FK on every table gives each lab its own copy of the same antibody in the catalog. That defeats the v2 cross-lab matching the FK is meant to enable, and forces lab into every catalog unique constraint.
- status and end_date on User can't represent a rotator who belongs to two labs.
- FKs alone don't stop cross-lab references (a StockItem in lab A sitting in a Location of lab B) or unscoped queries.

Problems with people:
- On the Quartzy side, requested_by and User.email can be null.
- Former members never log in but still own history.
- The custodian field has no way to express shared lab stock, or the PI pool that receives leavers' items.
issues.fix:
Make the catalog global: VendorFamily, Vendor, Product, SupplierProduct, ProductCode and Lot. Add an optional LabProduct overlay for min stock, synonyms and notes.

Put the lab FK on tenant data only: Location, StockItem, Hold, StockEvent, QuartzyLab (and through it OrderRequest), Notification, DuplicateCheck, PolicySetting, HistoryClaim and AskThread.

Add Membership(user, lab, role, status, start_date, end_date) to replace User.status and end_date. Enforce scoping with for_lab managers, a request.lab middleware, and a clean()/service check that item.lab == location.lab. Give each lab a 'Lab stock' pool person, used as custodian for shared and orphaned items.

PersonAlias resolution:
- Match on Quartzy user id first, then lowercased email, then send to a manual queue.
- Former members get inactive placeholder users with no login.
- If requested_by is null, use created_by.
- If the requester is unmapped, still send the alert to requested_by.email and queue the mapping.
- requested_for exists only in the app (set from claims or alerts), never parsed from the payload.
issues.evidence: public-api.yaml: OrderRequestWithType.requested_by is nullable; User.email and last_name are nullable. The critique asked for a lab FK on 'Location, StockItem, Person and visibility', not on the catalog.

issues.section: §2 Notifications (signed links); §6 Notification; §8 step 2
issues.problem:
Opening a confirm page on GET and acting only on POST is right, but the token handling is underspecified.
- Notification stores the signed token itself, so anyone who can read the database or the admin holds live action links.
- Single use, scope and expiry are undefined.
- The confirm page is exactly where an htmx hx-trigger='load' or a JS auto-submit would bring back mutation on prefetch.
- Tokens in URLs end up in Caddy access logs and error-tracking breadcrumbs.

Multi-item flows break down too. A monthly claim email with 20 items would mean 20 confirm pages. Links to login-required pages open in Outlook's in-app browser, which has no session.
issues.fix:
- **Token:** TimestampSigner(salt='labstock.action.v1').sign_object({n: notification_id, r: recipient_id, k: nonce}). Store only the nonce, and rotate it to revoke. max_age is 14 days.
- **Single use:** the POST sets acted_at under select_for_update; a repeat shows 'already recorded'. The outcome stays editable later after login.
- **Confirm page:** a plain <form method=post> reading 'Recording as <name>, not you?', with no htmx or JS triggers. Tests check that GET and HEAD never change data and that the template has no hx-trigger.
- **Claim list:** the email link opens a session scoped to that person's claim list for 7 days, and its htmx POSTs are authorized by that scope. Search and every other page still require login.
- **Logging:** strip tokens from Caddy logs (filter encoder) and Sentry (before_send). Keep Django's default same-origin Referrer-Policy.
issues.evidence: Plan §6: 'Notification: recipient, kind, signed token, sent/acted'. Plan §10 tests cover only 'expiry, tampering, and GET never mutates'.

issues.section: §5 Frontend (htmx + Alpine); §8 step 1 Scaffold
issues.problem:
Django 6 has built-in CSP, but the plan never turns it on, and the chosen frontend tools conflict with a strict policy.
- The standard Alpine build needs 'unsafe-eval'.
- htmx injects inline indicator styles.
- htmx evaluates hx-on attributes, event filters and js: values with eval unless allowEval is false.
- htmx's history cache keeps page HTML in localStorage (historyCacheSize defaults to 10), which leaks restricted pages on MVP-B's shared freezer tablets.

Claude Code will write inline Alpine with arrow functions and template literals, which the CSP build rejects. Retrofitting CSP after 100 templates is expensive.
issues.fix:
Decide at scaffold time. Either drop Alpine from MVP-A (htmx plus one small static ES module), or use @alpinejs/csp with Alpine.data components only.

In base.html, add an htmx-config meta tag: {allowEval: false, includeIndicatorStyles: false, historyCacheSize: 0}, and move the indicator CSS into the static stylesheet. Send CSRF through hx-headers on <body>. Set SECURE_CSP with a nonce-based script-src 'self', with no unsafe-eval or unsafe-inline. Enforce it in dev and tests too, so Playwright catches violations.
issues.evidence: alpinejs.dev/advanced/csp: the standard build needs utilities that 'violate the unsafe-eval Content Security Policy'; the CSP build rejects arrow functions, template literals, property assignments and globals. htmx docs: includeIndicatorStyles defaults to true; allowEval=false disables event filters, hx-on and js: values; historyCacheSize can be set to 0.

issues.section: §5 Compose services / Backups; §4 MVP-A Ops (heartbeat)
issues.problem:
The worker sends every email, so an in-app heartbeat can't report the worker's own death. If backups also run as Q2 schedules, one dead worker stops alerts, sync and backups together without a sound.

The restic password and the ESP and Quartzy secrets live only on the server. If the server is lost, the off-site backup can't be decrypted.

postgres:18 moved its data directory: PGDATA now lives under /var/lib/postgresql/18/docker, and the volume belongs at /var/lib/postgresql. The classic compose mount `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`, which Claude Code will write by default, either fails or leaves the data outside the named volume.
issues.fix:
Use an external dead-man's switch (healthchecks.io free tier, or self-hosted) with three checks:
- a Q2 heartbeat schedule every 5 min
- 'sync succeeded' after each lab sync
- 'backup succeeded' after restic

It emails both the owner and the deputy. The web app shows a banner when the last successful sync is more than 30 minutes old.

Run backups from a host systemd timer or cron job, or a supercronic sidecar, never from Django-Q2: `docker compose exec db pg_dump -Fc` (the v18 client), then restic. Keep the restic password, ESP key and Quartzy token in a password manager the deputy can open.

In compose.yaml, mount `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql`. The restore drill includes `docker compose down && up` and checks row counts.
issues.evidence: docker-library/postgres issue #1370 and the Docker forum: from 18, the VOLUME is /var/lib/postgresql and mounts at /var/lib/postgresql/data fail. Tech research: 'a dead worker silently stops all alerts'.

issues.section: §10 Verification
issues.problem: The listed tests run parsing and idempotency checks on static recorded fixtures. The sync's bugs live in sequences: page shifts, 404 tombstones, mass 404s, 429/5xx responses and timeouts, nullable fields, Q2 redelivery. Concurrent ledger writes, time-based rules and redaction across channels aren't tested either. And openapi-core validation against a spec full of additionalProperties:false will fail on harmless new fields.
issues.fix:
Add:
(1) A stateful fake Quartzy: a respx-mounted httpx transport over an in-memory list, configurable for page size, sort order, inserts during a scan, deletes, 404s and 429s. All sync tests use it.
(2) time-machine tests for arming, late alerts, nudges, digests and token expiry.
(3) Double-run and concurrent tests for the sync and send tasks.
(4) A TransactionTestCase with two DB connections writing to one StockItem.
(5) The redaction matrix.
(6) Q_CLUSTER sync=True in test settings.
(7) pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning for first-party modules, to catch 6.1→6.2 deprecations early.
(8) openapi-core validation with additionalProperties relaxed, plus a report of unknown fields.

Keep Playwright to the four listed flows.
issues.evidence: Plan §10 lists 'fixtures validated against public-api.yaml using openapi-core' and 'sync idempotency: a second run changes nothing' only. The spec marks Money, User and the request bodies additionalProperties:false.

issues.section: §4 Roadmap estimates (Phase 0, MVP-A)
issues.problem:
Phase 0's '~15–25 h, mostly no code' covers the probe, a full export, anonymized fixtures, a normalization ruleset and a classified baseline; realistically that is 25–40 h. MVP-A's 100–200 h has no line for:
- per-person spreadsheet cleanup: about 30 files in different layouts, many of them box grids, at 0.5–2 h each is 15–60 h
- pilot fixes during shadow and go-live

Summing step-level ranges gives about 150–300 h.

Give each step in §8 an hour range:
- scaffold + core: 10–15
- catalog: 15–25
- sync: 20–35
- deploy, ops and email: 10–20
- guard: 25–40
- inventory, claims and asks: 25–40

result.verdict: Sound research base and architecture. As written, though, MVP-A is mainly a post-purchase guard and won't reliably cut duplicate spend. In a self-ordering lab the 5-minute-poll email often lands after checkout; Quartzy Connect even creates the request on the vendor page. Purchases and stock that never touch Quartzy have no way in, and several flows (post-order variant, stale nudges, claims) assume ORDERED/RECEIVED statuses that non-admin self-orderers can't or don't set. Fixes: pull cheap pre-order hooks into MVP-A (catalog/URL search, address-bar keyword, 1–2 min polling, alerts to both requesters, an alert that asks 'already ordered?'), add a quick-add and box-registration path, key claims and nudges off request age, make a named wet-lab co-owner a Phase 0 exit criterion, and announce each rule only when its tool ships. That adds roughly 30–50 focused hours to MVP-A, partly offset by the cuts listed. With these changes a measurable reduction within two to three quarters is plausible; without them, expect better visibility but little measurable change in spend.

issues.section: §2 Ordering model; §4 MVP-A Duplicate guard; §7 Sync cadence and Alert email; §4 v1 extension
issues.problem: MVP-A's guard is mostly a post-purchase rescue. Self-orderers often check out minutes after creating the Quartzy request, and Quartzy Connect creates the request on the vendor page itself. A 5-minute poll plus email therefore usually lands after checkout. The only pre-order defence is a search habit with nothing in the buying flow to trigger it until the v1 extension. Purchases outside Quartzy are invisible. The plan doesn't measure this gap, has no rule for when to pull the extension forward, and alerts only the second requester.
issues.fix:
(a) Phase 0 timing check: from a real request export (check its columns for Ordered/Received dates) compute the Submitted→Ordered gap and the gap between paired duplicates. Flag after-the-fact entries (Submitted≈Ordered). Ask 5 frequent orderers how their last 3 orders went (Quartzy first or vendor first, Connect, P-card, institutional portal). Have the PI's admin estimate the share of spend outside Quartzy from one quarter of P-card/departmental statements. During shadow mode, re-fetch each new request at +5, +15 and +60 min to time CREATED→ORDERED.
(b) MVP-A pre-order hooks (~1 day): a GET /s?q= search that accepts a raw catalog # or a pasted vendor product URL, with server-side per-vendor URL patterns (Thermo, Fisher, Sigma, CST, Abcam, NEB, ATCC, IDT, Qiagen, VWR) that v1's extension reuses later. Add a one-click setup for an address-bar keyword ('ls 2118S' via Chrome/Edge site search or a Firefox keyword bookmark) and a bookmarklet (selection or page URL, opens a new tab; test it on those sites because strict CSP can block bookmarklets). Put both on the cheat sheet and in every alert footer.
(c) Latency: poll the new-ids page every 1–2 min during lab hours (07–20), every 10 min otherwise; if needed, refresh open requests every 2 h to stay within ~300 calls/h. Enable the order-request.created webhook as a hint once public HTTPS exists, and add guard latency to the hosting criteria.
(d) Recipients: on an open-request match, email both requesters, because the earlier one may not have checked out yet and can offer to share. On a bought-before match, a one-tap 'Ask Lee if she still has it' turns Lee's yes/no into a claim. For in-the-lab matches, email only the requester; the owner is contacted when the requester taps Borrow.
(e) One alert per request that branches on the person's answer, not on Quartzy status. Subject: 'Before you order: Priya has CST 2118S (GAPDH 14C10) in -20 B'. Body: the request line, then the best match with owner, location, date and why it matched (exact cat # / other pack size), then 'Have you placed the vendor order yet?'
- Not yet: [Borrow from Priya] [Share Raj's order] [Cancel my Quartzy request (opens Quartzy)]
- Yes: [I'll cancel with the vendor] (shows that vendor's cancel contact and the Quartzy confirmation #) [Keep it, offer the spare]
- Always: [Not the same thing] [Need my own: lot / application / urgent / other]
Store the answer as alert_in_time. No follow-up emails; unresolved alerts appear in the personal digest.
(f) Decision rule: if alert_in_time stays below ~40% and search-before-buy stays low after 6 live weeks, make a minimal URL-pattern extension the first v1 item.
(g) Scope the PI rule: 'Antibodies, kits, enzymes, cytokines/inhibitors, cell lines or anything over (e.g.) $250: search LabStock before checkout, or create the Quartzy request and wait for LabStock's email.' For in-scope requests, send a one-line 'No match, clear to order' receipt for the first 8 weeks so silence isn't ambiguous.
issues.evidence: Quartzy Connect (help article 55420967896475, Sep 2026): any user can create requests from vendor pages, with no documented duplicate check. The API exposes only the current status and updated_at; the request export filters by status-change date (234660807). Plan §7 polls every 5 min and alerts 'within one sync cycle'; §2 defers the extension to v1. Bookmarklets can be blocked by strict site CSP ([Ben Nadel/Loggly](https://www.bennadel.com/blog/3997-converting-my-loggly-search-bookmarklets-into-an-unpacked-chrome-extension.htm), [Mozilla bug 866522](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=866522)), so the address-bar keyword is the reliable path.

issues.section: §4 Phase 0 steps 2–3; §4 MVP-A Claim your history and stale nudges; §7 Candidates and Alert
issues.problem: Several flows treat Quartzy statuses as ground truth, but only Lab Admins can Mark Ordered, and members can cancel only their own New requests. So in a lab where everyone orders, either most people are Lab Admins or bought items sit in CREATED. That breaks: the post-order variant (keyed on ORDERED); stale nudges (ORDERED >21 d); claim-your-history and bought-before (keyed on RECEIVED); 'I'll cancel' (a member can't cancel once a request leaves New). Shared logins used to save seats would make requested_by, and so alert routing, meaningless.
issues.fix:
Phase 0 (Lab Admin + bioinformatician, ~1 h): list each member's role and whether they have their own seat. From the export, measure the % of requests that reach RECEIVED, the % stuck in CREATED for over 30 days, and the median CREATED→ORDERED time. Extend the stale cleanup to CREATED/APPROVED requests older than 30 days. Keep the Lab Admin list in PolicySetting, since the API can't return roles. Design changes:
- Treat a request as 'probably bought' when it isn't CANCELLED and is more than 14 days old, whatever its status. Claims, bought-before candidates and leaver orphans all use this.
- Stale nudge when a request isn't RECEIVED or CANCELLED 21 days after requested_at: [It arrived] [Still waiting] [Never ordered, cancel (opens Quartzy)]. Record the answer in the app.
- Cancel buttons name who can act ('Ask <Lab Admin> to cancel' when the requester can't).
- Fix shared logins before MVP-A (ToS §3.2(a), attribution).
issues.evidence: [Quartzy article 115000426253](https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000426253-Lab-Admin-vs-Lab-Member-privileges-explained) (updated 2026-06-24): Mark as Ordered is Admin-only; members cancel or edit only their own requests in New; both roles can Mark Received. The plan keys the post-order variant and 21-day nudge on ORDERED, and claims and look-back candidates on RECEIVED.

issues.section: §4 MVP-A Spreadsheet import / Claim your history; §4 v1 outside-Quartzy log; §9 Amnesty
issues.problem: Much of the hidden stock never went through Quartzy: items from previous labs, collaborator cell lines and plasmids (often under MTA), lab-made reagents, vendor samples, P-card buys, leavers' leftovers. MVP-A's only path for these is the developer scripting someone's spreadsheet, and most bench people don't keep one. Phase 0 announces 'log non-Quartzy purchases', but the form arrives in v1. Claim-your-history covers only the claimer's own requests, so shared and departed members' items go unclaimed.
issues.fix:
Move into MVP-A (S, ~2–3 days):
(1) A desk 'Add what I have' form. Fields: name (typeahead over products seeded from Quartzy history), type, source (previous lab / collaborator / lab-made / gift or sample / outside purchase), coarse location, custodian = me, visibility defaulting to ask-first. Collaborator + MTA defaults to restricted, which still shows that the item exists. Vendor, cat # and photo are optional. Outside purchases also create OrderRequest(source=outside), so the guard sees them.
(2) 'Register a box': owner, location, type tags and a lid/contents photo. A registered box counts as visible and is searchable by owner and type; itemize later (v1 photo intake can fill contents).
(3) Phase 0 collects lab-wide registers first (LN2/cell-line log, primer, plasmid and antibody lists, shared enzyme box), then personal sheets into one import template. Per-person cleanup scripts are for legacy sheets only.
(4) Claims get an 'It's in the shared stock' option, plus a lab-pool list of durable items requested by departed members in the last 24 months, which champions work through during the amnesty.
(5) Amnesty is a freezer-by-freezer walk: every box gets an owner sticker and a box registration (~30 s/box). The PI announces up front that unregistered boxes found at the next clean-out go to an 'unclaimed' shelf for 4 weeks, then to the lab pool.
issues.evidence: Plan Phase 0 rule 'log non-Quartzy purchases' vs §4 v1 'log for purchases outside Quartzy'. The research synthesis rates that log S complexity. dupes_adoption: lab-made reagents are 'the most hidden personal inventory'; MTA/collaborator materials must not be auto-shared.

issues.section: §4 Phase 0; §9 Roles; §12 Open items
issues.problem: Phase 0 and shadow mode need wet-lab judgement the system owner doesn't have. Someone has to decide which baseline clusters are real duplicates and which are legitimate repeats, which Quartzy Types are durable, whether two GAPDH clones count as one, who owns which rack, and how freezer sessions run. The plan defers the data steward ('don't block MVP-A') and gives champions no tasks or time. That is the route to the superuser trap: the bioinformatician becomes the lab's data-entry clerk and arbiter.
issues.fix:
Phase 0 exit criterion: the PI names a wet-lab co-owner (lab manager or senior tech) and 3–4 champions, each with ~1 h/week for 10 weeks. RACI:
- PI: rule scope (types, $ threshold), default visibility = ask-first with a 'registered ≠ shared' guarantee, amnesty dates and the unclaimed-items policy, privacy commitments, hardware budget, launch talk.
- Co-owner: map Quartzy Types to ItemTypes and set the durable list and look-back windows; review the top ~40 baseline clusters by $; label shadow matches 15 min/week; curate vendor families and equivalences; write the coarse location list (units, shelves/racks, owners).
- Quartzy Lab Admin: role/seat audit, stale cleanup, native-warning test, webhook setup later.
- Bioinformatician: probe, export, baseline notebook, Quartzy/IT emails (SMTP sender, hostname), imports.
- Champions: pilot users, recruit their bay, run freezer walks, keep the friction log.
Move 'data steward' from §12 into Phase 0.
issues.evidence: Plan §12 lists 'Who is the long-term data steward?' as not blocking MVP-A, and §9 names champions without tasks. dupes_adoption pitfall: 'The superuser trap: if the lab manager or a bioinformatician becomes everyone's data-entry clerk, usage stats look healthy while the system depends on one person.'

issues.section: §2 Notifications; §4 MVP-A Check-before-you-buy (Ask the lab) and digests; §5 Architecture
issues.problem: Email is the only channel, but nothing makes sure alerts arrive, get read, and can be acted on in one step. Mail from a new self-hosted sender often lands in Junk/Other. Outcome pages behind a login code will get few taps, and the metrics depend on those outcomes. A generic Monday digest plus lab-wide 'Ask the lab' blasts invite a mail filter that will also swallow alerts. The 'I have it' reply implies inbound-mail parsing that isn't in the architecture.
issues.fix:
Phase 0 IT ask: send via the institution's relay or an approved provider, with SPF/DKIM on a trusted domain. Test inbox placement and delay for 3 people on desktop and phone. At launch, ask everyone to mark the first email Not Junk / Always Focused.
- Signed links act as the auth for one action (recipient + object + action, single-use, 14-day expiry). Outcome and borrow pages need no login.
- Two senders: alerts@ for personal, action-needed mail and news@ for digests and asks, with distinct subject prefixes.
- The Monday digest is per person and skipped when empty: your unresolved alerts, borrow requests, items to claim or place.
- 'Ask the lab' sends per-recipient emails with a signed [I have it] button (no reply parsing), max 1 ask/person/day, batched twice daily unless marked urgent.
- Don't duplicate Quartzy's own status emails. Cap non-alert mail at ~3/person/week.
issues.evidence: Plan: 'Monday digest email for everyone'; 'an "I have it" reply creates a pending claim'; no inbound-mail component in §5. Quartzy already emails requesters on approved/ordered/cancelled/backordered/received when enabled ([article 233072048](https://support.quartzy.com/hc/en-us/articles/233072048)).

issues.section: §4 MVP-A Minimal inventory / Claim your history
issues.problem: 'Still have it (pick a box)' needs a box-level location tree that nobody is assigned to build in MVP-A; freezer templates are MVP-B. On amnesty day, claims stall at 'pick a box' for hundreds of boxes the app doesn't know. Monthly claim batches grow large and get ignored.
issues.fix:
Seed a coarse tree in MVP-A (room → unit → shelf/rack, with owners) from the co-owner's 1-hour walk via CSV. Auto-create per-person 'unsorted' containers per temperature (e.g. 'Priya -20 unsorted').
- Claim pickers default to my containers, offer 'place it later' (the digest reminds you) and let people create a box inline (name + unit + shelf).
- Print human-readable short-ID box labels now. MVP-B adds QR stickers with the same IDs once the hostname is fixed.
- Sort the claim list by price, show progress, allow 'done for now'.
- Surface new claim items weekly (7 days after receipt or 21 days after request), not monthly.
issues.evidence: Plan §4 MVP-A has 'a box-level Location tree' and 'Still have it (pick a box)'; 'Freezer templates for bulk-creating shelves, racks and boxes' is MVP-B; claims 'repeat monthly'.

issues.section: §9 Metrics; §4 Phase 0 step 4; §7 $ avoided
issues.problem: The baseline will over-count: two people can legitimately need the same antibody, consumables repeat, projects differ. An analyzer run by a non-wet-lab owner can't tell these apart. Real clusters may number only tens a year, with seasonal swings (new students, grant cycles), so 'duplicate rate vs baseline' can stay noise for months. WAU and median search time are vanity or hard to measure. Neither tracks the two mechanisms that decide success: did the alert arrive in time, and did people search first.
issues.fix:
Report the baseline twice: an upper bound (all clusters) and a reviewed figure (co-owner labels the top ~40 by $). Break both down by bucket and time gap. Compare like-for-like quarters with the same analyzer version, and publish counts plus the list, not percentages. Dashboard:
1. reviewed avoidable-duplicate $ per quarter vs the same quarter a year earlier
2. alert_in_time rate
3. search-before-buy rate for in-scope requests: a search resolving to that product by the requester in the prior 24 h, stored as a boolean on DuplicateCheck and shown only in aggregate
4. coverage: % of in-scope requests from the last 24 months claimed or resolved, and boxes with an owner per freezer
5. asks that ended in a borrow
6. precision per tier
Count $ avoided only if the same person makes no equivalent request within 30 days. Count post-order cancels only when the person confirms the vendor cancelled. Drop WAU and median search time; keep the <10 s / ≤2 taps targets as pilot usability tests.
issues.evidence: Plan §9 metrics: duplicate rate vs baseline, $ avoided, put-away %, weekly active users, median search time. Research: hard numbers on duplicate spend are scarce, so measure the lab's own baseline and count savings conservatively.

issues.section: §9 Privacy; §4 MVP-A PI dashboard v0 / digests; §7 Alert
issues.problem: Several features make the app look like purchase monitoring: the PI's daily 'new lab orders' digest, per-person PI views, logged searches, and per-person 'ordered anyway + reason' records. Members then stop tapping honest outcomes or move purchases outside Quartzy, which blinds the guard. In Germany/EU, monitoring-capable software can also need staff-council sign-off.
issues.fix:
Put these commitments in privacy.md and the launch talk:
- The PI sees lab-level metrics and custodianship (who holds what), never individual behaviour (searches, alert outcomes, override reasons).
- No per-person duplicate counts.
- Search logs are kept 30 days for the search-before-buy flag, then deleted.
- Override reasons are a pick-list used only for tuning.
- Lenders are celebrated by name only with opt-in.
- Every alert footer says 'Only you receive this; the PI sees lab totals only.'
Replace the PI's daily digest with a weekly lab-level summary: duplicates caught, $ avoided, top categories, and unresolved high-value flags without names.
issues.evidence: Plan: 'optional daily "new lab orders" digest for the PI'; 'per-person views for the PI and admin only'. Research: per-person dashboards used to shame lead to gaming and hiding; BetrVG §87(1) Nr. 6 (DE) co-determination for monitoring-capable software.

issues.section: §4 Phase 0 step 1; §9 Sequence
issues.problem: The PI announces all five rules in week 0, but search arrives with MVP-A (100–200 h, likely months part-time), put-away with MVP-B, and the outside-purchase log with v1. Rules with no tool behind them lose credibility before launch. The sequence also has no post-launch follow-up session (where workarounds surface), no protected time for the amnesty, and no onboarding for the constant flow of rotators.
issues.fix:
Tie each announcement to shipped features.
- Phase 0 lab meeting: the project, the anonymized baseline (top duplicated products, $), the asks for registers and spreadsheets, Quartzy hygiene.
- MVP-A launch meeting (10-min live demo searching items the audience names): the rules that now have tools: search first for in-scope items, a reason on a strong match, log outside purchases and gifts.
- Amnesty fortnight 2 weeks after launch: one lab-meeting slot becomes a 'freezer hour', with a by-bay tally of boxes registered.
- Put-away rule at MVP-B launch.
- Follow-up at 3–4 weeks: announce the top 3 friction-log fixes.
- Then a 2-minute monthly PI slot (trend, $ avoided, borrow stories).
- Add LabStock to new-member onboarding: a 10-min tour plus a first registration.
issues.evidence: Plan Phase 0 step 1 announces 'confirm a location when things arrive' and 'log non-Quartzy purchases' in weeks 0–1; put-away is MVP-B and the outside log v1. Research: the 2–4-week follow-up session is 'the most valuable session and the one most often skipped'.

issues.section: §2 Item types; §7 Candidates (look-back windows); §6 ItemType
issues.problem: The type order is right, but 'reagents' is vague, and 'chemicals last' will probably sweep in bioactive small molecules/inhibitors, cytokines/growth factors, recombinant proteins and siRNA/sgRNA. These are $150–600 items kept in personal -20/-80 boxes and a classic duplicate class, yet they're missing from the 24-month look-back list. Shared lab stocks (common buffers, media, competent cells, the shared enzyme and secondary-antibody boxes) have no type, custodian or claim option, although 'we're out, I'll order' is a common simultaneous duplicate.
issues.fix: Tier 1 = antibodies (primary and secondary), kits (including instrument kits), enzymes, bioactive small molecules/inhibitors, cytokines/growth factors/recombinant proteins, siRNA/sgRNA, FBS/serum lots. Split chemicals into bioactives (tier 1, matched on vendor cat # + CAS) and bulk/hazardous (last, EHS). Apply the 24-month windows to all of tier 1. Add a generic 'Lab-made / shared stock' type with a lab-pool custodian and a named steward per shared item, and rank shared stock first in search. Keep cell lines second (LN2-log import gives early coverage) and oligos third. Equipment stays out of scope.
issues.evidence: Plan §7: 24-month windows only for 'antibodies, kits, enzymes and cell lines; none for consumables'; §2 order ends with 'chemicals'.

issues.section: §4 MVP-B Cycle counting / Bench pages / Labels; §6 Hold; §4 Phase 0 step 5
issues.problem: Some MVP-B pieces won't be used in a lab without a full-time manager. Random-box weekly counts land on people who don't own those boxes. 'Used some' produces meaningless data. Labels per tube are unrealistic. Hold isn't needed before borrow/lend. The Phase 0 barcode census serves v1 scanning.
issues.fix: Replace random cycle counts with custodian self-checks (the digest asks each person to confirm 1–2 of their own boxes a month, one tap each) plus a full recount at the annual clean-out/defrost. Bench buttons: Opened · Running low · Empty · Moved · Discard. Labels: box-level by default, with item labels only for antibodies, kits, cell-line boxes and items ≥$X. Move Hold to v1 (borrow/lend) and the barcode census to the start of v1 scanning.
issues.evidence: Plan MVP-B: 'the digest assigns 2 random boxes per freezer each week'; bench buttons include 'Used some'. Research: item labels for high-value/unique items, shelf/bin codes for consumables.

issues.section: §4 Phase 0 step 2 (Quartzy hygiene)
issues.problem: The 'optional approvals' lever contradicts the locked no-approver decision. Nothing tests whether the native duplicate warning fires in mobile and Quartzy Connect. The one in-Quartzy nudge that needs no approver isn't considered. And after the switch, Quartzy's Inventory module will keep showing stale 'Found in Inventory' hits in the lookup Phase 0 tells people to use.
issues.fix: Remove the approvals lever. Park it as a fallback after 6 months of metrics, needing the user's sign-off. The Lab Admin tests the native warning in web, mobile and Connect with a deliberate repeat catalog #. Optional 4-week trial: an org-level required single-select custom request field 'Checked LabStock? (yes / need my own / no)', which prompts at the moment of request in web and Connect. Caveats: it needs an Org Admin, the API can't read it (a nudge, not a metric), and it disables QBot. Define Quartzy Inventory's end state: after a month of MVP-B put-away, export a backup, then bulk-delete via the Excel 'Delete? (Y/N)' import so the lookup stops showing stale stock.
issues.evidence: Required custom request fields support Text/Single Select/Checkbox/Date (4407114944155), aren't exposed by the API, disable QBot auto-requests (38547448619547), and are managed by Org Admins (14740305537947). Connect auto-fills custom fields (55420967896475). Bulk delete via import (234450488).

issues.section: §4 MVP-A launch scope; §4 v1 oligo registry; §7 Noise control (shadow mode)
issues.problem: Most of MVP-A's value goes to the PI. Bench members get personal benefit only from search, and the first visible alert waits 2–4 weeks of shadow mode. The cheapest personal win for a bioinformatician-built tool, 'has anyone already got a primer for this?', sits in v1.
issues.fix: (1) Launch with 24 months of 'Bought before' already searchable, and demo it live. (2) Gate T1 exact-catalog matches against open requests after 1 week of shadow. This is Quartzy's own rule extended across formats and Labs. Keep 2–4 weeks for T2 and received-history matches. (3) Fast-follow after MVP-A (~2–3 days): a primer finder. Import IDT order spec sheets and lab primer lists, then search by name, gene or sequence (exact / reverse-complement / substring). The full oligo registry stays in v1.
issues.evidence: Plan: 'shadow mode for 2–4 weeks before alerts go live'; the oligo registry with sequence search is v1. Research (Dirnagl & Przesdzing): early users become 'avid supporters' who win over skeptics.

must_keep: Baseline duplicate analysis classified by why Quartzy missed each case; it is the 'before' number and calibrates the matcher
Shadow mode with per-tier precision gates, one-tap 'not a duplicate' pair suppression, recurring-consumable suppression, and no alerts during backfill
